lawyer:
Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh with Imranul Kabir with Mejbahur Rahman with Khandaker Reza-e-Razib with Samia Afroj Khan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate ----- For the Respondents (ACC).
parties:
Golam Nabi and another -----Petitioners
Vs.
Anti Corruption Commissions and others -----Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: These Rules issued in Writ Petition No. 7265 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7266 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7267 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7268 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7269 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7270 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7271 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7272 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7273 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7274 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7275 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7276 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7277 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 7278 of 2008 and Writ Petition No. 7336 of 2008 sent by his Lordship, the Chief Justice of Bangladesh for disposal are taken together for analogous hearing as the matter involved in those Writ Petitions are identical one arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 140 date 29- 3-2007 corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 25 of 2007 punishable under sections 40911 09 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 2. In fact, all these Rules under article 102 (2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the accused-petitioners challenging the order of sanction for prosecution of the accused-persons in ACC GR Case No. 25 of 2007 arising out of Motijheel PS Case No. 140 dated 29-3-2007 punishable under section 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 are disposed of in one judgment since all these arises out of same ACC GR case and the matter of adjudication of all these writ petitions are identical in nature we are going to write single judgment which will govern all these writ petitions referred to above. 

 3. The facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule is that the petitioner along with another were implicated in Motijheel PS Case No. 140 dated 29-03-2007 corresponding to ACC GR No. 25 of 2007 for committing the offence punishable under section 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Investigating Officer, having been authorized by the Commission investigated the case and recommended to stand trial of the accused-petitioner for committing the offence mentioned in the police report with a further prayer of according sanction as required under section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with rule 15 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rule, 2007. 

 5. Mr Taposh further submits that in the instant case admittedly, sanction has been accorded by one of the member named Md Habibur Rahman which also stands against the mandatory provision laid down in section 32(1) and (2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 because the very sanctioning power for prosecution has been given by the legislature to the Commission, not any member of the Commission as such sanction for prosecution as required by law has not been duly complied with. Emphasising much importance on this argument supported by a Judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7242 of 2008 the learned Advocate has prayed to make this rule absolute without any further discussion. 

 7. Mr Taposh goes to argue that this provision incorporating in this statute especially in the 'Form-3' of the Rules, 2007 is not an idle provision, which can be ignored by the prosecution taking the matter in his own manner in order to regulate the proceeding of the Court. In support of his contention the learned advocate has referred a decision of a case Anti-Corruption Commission vs Sheikh Hasina Wazed reported in 60 DLR (AD) 172 where their lordships of the Apex Court has made a positive observation that satisfaction as has been deserved is the exclusive satisfaction of the Commission and in the instant case since no such satisfaction is available the mechanical sanction accorded by the commission in 'Form-3' is in the eye of law is not a sanction at all. Moreover the number of case as has been started arising out of the self same occurrence is also against the provision of law, which can also vitiate the trial in order to avoid unnecessary suffering to the accused-persons. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent (ACC) has strongly opposed the Rules alleging that the writ petitions challenging the initiation of criminal proceeding pending before the Special Judge-3, Dhaka as a special case cannot be brought within the mischief of writ jurisdiction because these tactics has totally been disapproved by the Appellant Division in a case Chairman, Anti-Corruption Commission vs Enayetur Rahman reported in 64 DLR (AD) 14 where their lordships have made the following observation- 

 9. Relying on the above decision of the Apex Court the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission respondent No.2 has also taken us in the decision of a case Habibur Rahman Mollah vs State reported in 61 DLR (HD) 1 and that judgment has been affirmed by the Appellate Division reported in 62 DLR (AD) 233. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 has quoted the decision of Habibur Rahman Mollah's case in appearing para 18-22. 

 15. The above provision as laid down in section 18 has clearly empowered any member of the Commission to perform the duty of the Commission as assigned. In the instant case, admittedly one of the members of the Commission has been empowered to accord sanction on behalf of the commission as such the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner finds no leg to stand upon. 

 16. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2 further submits that the observation made in Mollah's case reported in 61 DLR 1 has been already affirmed by the Appellate Division is enough to make the Rule discharged because the mandatory provision of sanction for taking cognisance in one occasion relying upon a decision of a case Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 has also contributed much to dispose of all these Rules ignoring the decision of Writ Petition No. 7242 of 2008 where all those decisions of the Apex Court has not been referred. 

 17. Moreover, Mr Khan did not fail to point out that since the instant case there is no difference of opinion, rather an identical matter there are two judgments over the same case one is reported in 15 ELC 464 and another unreported case of Writ Petition No. 7242 of 2008 as such this Bench is absolutely at liberty to dispose of the matter following the decision of the Apex Court of the country over the same matter. Even any one of those two decisions may be adopted which will prevail. 

 19. It will not be out of place to mention that so far the sanction for prosecution as required under section 32(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 we are of opinion that in Habibur Rahman Mollas case the matter has elaborately discussed and decided where one of us was author Judge and their lordship of the Apex Court has affirmed that judgment, making no change therein as such Mollah s Judgment reported in 61 DLR 1 affirmed by Apex Court reported in 62 DLR (AD) 233 has become the judgment of the apex Court of the Country; so there can be no scope to go against the decision of the Apex Court over the self same matter. 

 20. Be the case as it may we have gone through the decision of a case Chairman, Anti- Corruption Commission vs Enayetur Rahman reported in 64 DLR (AD) 14 where their lordships have absolutely ousted the jurisdiction of the writ Court to quash the criminal proceeding pending before the Special Judge Court unless any vires of law is found to have been challenged. 

 21. In the instant case no vires of law has been challenged we find no way but to follow the decision of the Apex Court and the opinion and decision given in Writ Petition arising out of same ACC GR reported in 15 BLC 464 we must echo the voice of the Apex Court reported in 64 DLR (AD) 14 and also to say with reference to the provision laid down in section 18 of the Anti- Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 that sanction for prosecution accorded by one member of the Commission duly authorized by the Commission is enough to prosecute the accused of the schedule offence since this matter has already been settled in the case Habibur Rahman Mollah vs State affirmed by the Appellate Division, referred to above we find no scope to re-open the argument for anyone's benefit. 

 23. In the result, the Rules mentioned in title page arising out of the Special Case No. 16 of 2007 corresponding to ACC OR No. 25 of 2007 and Motijheel PS Case No. 140 dated 29-3-2007 are discharged.
